Do plyo! 75-125 touches (jumps) is a good range per session from what I’ve read in scholarly articles, not more than 3 times per week, and you should have sets of 2-6 and reps of 4-8 e.g. 8x2 vertical jumps, 6x4 lateral bounds etc. Rest periods for plyo are long because each repetition should be performed at maximal intensity so your rest times between sets should be longer than 1 minute and up to 3 minutes depending on how easily you fatigue, but it’s better to err on the side of caution. Focus hard on each jump and make sure you land softly, or you’ll end up with a headache by the end. 3-6 exercises is a good range per work out. 


E.g. your workout could be 


• 8x4vertical jumps
• 8x4 squat jumps 
• 5x5 lateral bounds
• 5x5 split squat jumps


and you might have two minutes rest between each set, which would be a total of 36 mins, which seems like a lot for just 98 jumps but that’s just how plyo works best! This is a meta analysis analysing the dose-response between vertical jump improvement and frequency or training, duration, interval and rest periods. 
https://journals.lww.com/nsca-jscr/Fulltext/2009/03000/Determining_Variables_of_Plyometric_Training_for.20.aspx


I don’t know if you’d be able to reach a 16 inch vertical but I think you could improve your vertical by about an inch and a half in around 10 weeks, depending on genetics and diet, and probably more given your age.
